historical_record.description: Built by the Western Pacific Railway as one of the corrugated steel structures the railroads put up cheaply for new tenants after the earthquake; designed by the company's chief engineer V. G. Bogue and built by Thomas H. Day & Sons. Long the home of the Union Machine Shop, and the only one of these buildings known to survive in the survey area. Engineered by the Western Pacific engineering office.

The city bought this building in the late 1960s for its Neighborhood Arts Program. It became the SoMa Cultural Center, home to a mural resource centre, a costume bank and technical services for artists, and was renamed SOMArts by the 1990s.

historic_survey.status_code_meaning: California Historical Resource Status Codes: a 1 or 2 means listed or formally determined eligible, a 3 means the survey judged it eligible, a 5 means locally significant, a 6 that it was found ineligible, and a 7 that it was not evaluated.
